status: PROPOSED, awaiting the user's approval; nothing here is frozen and no model has run
indices: 0-based design indices; the paper counts from 1

proposals.justification: Fixed before any data (brief Sec. 5.4); the paper reports positional predictions distributed near the positional index.

value.definition: s_min = max(Q, floor), Q = upper order statistic at level 0.99 of S over no-patch runs of the same cell on split A

proposals.justification: Anchored to no-patch runs: at most 1% of unpatched runs, whose answer lies outside the three candidate positions, would count as resolved. The floor keeps q from being a ratio of tiny masses: a resolved case puts at least 10% of the entity mass on the three candidates.

The profile bands are kappa*d wide on each side; d >= 0.20 gives bands of at least 0.05 on the T scale (range 1/3 to 1), five times the proposed dtype tolerance and above the expected sampling error of T_W from 200 split-B cases (about 0.02).

value.source: resolved q-vectors of split B, selected cell
value.statistic: sup-norm difference of the two resample means
value.delta: upper order statistic at level 1 - false_invalid_rate

proposals.justification: As in brief Sec. 5.9. Because max is 1-Lipschitz in the sup-norm, a passed gate also bounds |T(mean q, confirmation) - T_W| by delta. A 5% false-INVALID rate costs a rerun in one of twenty drift-free confirmations. If fewer than N confirmation cases are resolved, the actual false-INVALID rate is above 5% (conservative toward INVALID).

proposals.tie_break: declared order c1, c2, c3, c4
proposals.justification: Middle i_P at n = 7. Lexical and reflexive targets at the nearest admissible distance, on opposite sides of i_P, so they are neither inside the positional window nor next to each other (the paper reports suppression when lexical and reflexive indices are close, Sec. 3.3). The native answer at an end group, where native retrieval is most reliable, to keep the yield high. The four cells are the mirror images of one layout. At n = 7 and w = 1 only four slots lie outside the window, so two of i_L, i_R and i_N are always adjacent.

Split A only ranks d across four cells. Split B fixes the anchors: with 200 cases the standard error of T_W is about 0.02, below the smallest band half-width 0.05, and delta is resampled at m = N = 200. Each base context gives one conflict run, three agreement runs and one no-patch run.

value.gated_scenario: exclusion when 70% of resolved cases conform, at the split-B unresolved rate
value.increase_rule: if the power is below 0.80 at N = 200, use the smallest N in (250, 300) that reaches it, decided at the freeze; if none does, STOP (gate 10)
value.reported_scenario: adequacy when 90% of resolved cases conform, at the split-B unresolved rate (reported, not gated; see PREFLIGHT_PLAN.md)

proposals.justification: The brief's orientation reproduces exactly with the existing helper (adequacy at true coverage 0.90: 0.831 at N = 150; exclusion at 0.70: 0.842 at N = 200). Both figures assume no unresolved case. Under the declared unresolved rule adequacy power falls steeply with unresolved cases (0.39 at N = 200 with 5% unresolved), so the adequacy scenario is reported for the user's decision rather than gated.
alpha/4 with alpha = 0.05 (brief Sec. 5.11), the same per-tail level as the profile intervals.

Agreement transfer: T_A should describe a response in which all three signals agree; the paper reports consistent answers when two mechanisms are aligned (App. D.1). Yield: with a cap of 2N generated contexts, a yield of at least 0.50 keeps N reachable. dtype: one fifth of the smallest band half-width (0.05), with identical resolution status and argmax labels in every sampled case.

The right panel of the paper's Figure 5 is the music task at t_entity = 2; App. A.1 reports lexical and reflexive balanced at t_entity = 2 on three-entity tasks and fixes the query entities to 1 and 3. On the two-entity boxes task t_entity = 2 is the last entity, where the lexical mechanism dominates.

The brief's minimum. The positional mechanism weakens in middle groups as n grows (App. A.3). If development averages at n = 7 are not mixed, no cell reaches d_min and the result is NOT_DECIDABLE_WITH_CURRENT_INTERVENTIONS (S1); raising n is then the user's decision, before split A is drawn.

value.convention: input of decoder block 18, Hugging Face hidden_states[18], as tasks/dist.py:221
value.check: pilot: at layer 18 the patched answer is the donor's answer copy at or below chance; at 19 it is the majority (App. D.2 criterion); otherwise STOP and return to the user

proposals.justification: The paper does not print l for gemma-2-2b-it. Figure 2 shows layer 18 with layers 16-18 carrying binding information, the blog places retrieval in layers 19-25, and the notebook uses 18; the command-line default is 17.
bfloat16 as in the upstream notebook (example.ipynb:152); eager attention because Gemma 2 uses logit soft-capping; the float32 reference serves gate 7.

value.also_required: identical entity argmax and identical greedy generation

proposals.justification: Gate 5: patching a prompt's own activation must reproduce its native output; the bound allows only bfloat16 kernel noise.

value.criterion: the first word of the decoded answer equals the target entity, case-insensitive
value.readout_agreement: the argmax over the n entity logits names the same entity
value.agreement_donors: native correctness recorded, not a population filter

proposals.justification: Stricter than upstream's substring checker; a case enters only if recipient and donor are both natively correct and the readout agrees with the generation (brief Sec. 5.3).

value.rule: keep only entities that are one token with a leading space in the pinned tokenizer; checked at gate 3 before any sampling
value.stop_if: any category keeps fewer than n + 2 entities

proposals.justification: Upstream asserts single-token entities (tasks/dist.py:271-273) instead of filtering; the gated tokenizer could not be checked in this pass.

value.note: disjoint blocks; each base context uses random.Random(seed)

proposals.justification: Confirmation uses fresh base contexts from disjoint seeds (brief Sec. 5.7).
